items.entity: design domain Ω (shape, aspect ratio, size)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 refers only to 'the full design domain Ω'. The shape and aspect ratio of the Fig. 1 domain are only visible in the figure. Sec. 4.1 says the dataset images are 64x64 (square), but the text never says Fig. 1 is a dataset sample rather than a generic sketch. No absolute dimensions are given; these only rescale the result.
readings: square, aspect ratio 1:1 (like the 64x64 dataset of Sec. 4.1)

items.entity: structured FE grid for the Fig. 1 example
items.description: No mesh is given for Fig. 1. Sec. 4.1 gives 64x64 images for the dataset but also says the load channels store a value at 'every node', so it is unclear whether 64x64 counts elements or nodes. The text also never says Fig. 1 uses this resolution.
readings: a grid matching a non-square domain, e.g. 128 x 64 elements

items.description: Sec. 2.1 says only 'a set of displacement boundary conditions'. Where they act is shown only in Fig. 1 (the Fig. 2 caption says BCs are drawn as colour lines and dots). Sec. 4.1 mentions 42+5 dataset scenarios but never describes them.
readings: left edge (symmetry line) plus bottom-right corner node (half-MBB)
bottom-left and bottom-right corner nodes (simply supported)
only part of an edge (e.g. middle half of the left edge) or isolated nodes

items.entity: displacement boundary conditions (which DOFs are fixed)
items.description: The text never says which displacement components are fixed at each support (clamp/pin vs roller). Per the Fig. 2 caption, figures show BCs as coloured lines and dots, but the text gives no colour legend.
readings: all supported nodes fixed in x and y
rollers: only u_x = 0 or only u_y = 0 at some supports
one pin (x and y fixed) plus one roller (only y fixed)

items.description: Sec. 2.1 and the Fig. 1 caption say only 'a given set of load' applied 'on the nodes of the domain'. The node is shown only by an arrow in Fig. 1. Sec. 4.1 says dataset loads sit on randomly chosen unconstrained boundary nodes. Readings are given as (x/L, y/H) from the bottom-left corner.

'A given set of load' (Fig. 1 caption) and 'loads are applied on ... nodes' (Sec. 4.1) do not say whether there is one concentrated nodal force, several forces, or a load spread over a boundary segment.
readings: single concentrated force at one node
two or more concentrated nodal forces in one load case
force spread uniformly over a few adjacent boundary nodes

items.description: The direction is shown only by the arrow in Fig. 1. Sec. 4.1 gives dataset angles in [0, π] with step π/6 but no reference axis or rotation sense. A downward load would fall outside [0, π] if angles are measured counter-clockwise (CCW) from +x.
No force magnitude is given for Fig. 1 or anywhere else in the text.
readings: F = 1000 N (or any other arbitrary value)

items.description: The Fig. 1 caption lists volume fraction as an input, but the text gives no value. The Sec. 4.1 dataset range [0.3, 0.5] with step 0.02 is not stated to apply to Fig. 1.
readings: another dataset grid value between 0.32 and 0.48 (step 0.02)

items.description: No material constants or thickness are given. Sec. 2.1 only mentions mechanical compliance, and Sec. 4.1 gives stress/strain-energy formulas without constants.
Poisson's ratio is not given anywhere in the text.

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: Not stated for the optimization solve. The only hint is the 2D von Mises formula in Sec. 4.1 (no σ33 term), which suggests plane stress, but it refers to the dataset's physical-field channels.
Sec. 2.1 says only 'with p > 1'. No value or continuation scheme is given.
readings: continuation from p = 1 up to p = 3

items.description: Sec. 2.1 (and Secs. 1 and 3.2) mention 'filters' only in general terms, as a binarization aid also used for the SIMP ground truth. The filter type is not given.
No filter radius is given anywhere in the text.
The lower bound of the SIMP interpolation is not given in Sec. 2.1 or anywhere else.

items.entity: optimizer, initial design and stopping criterion
items.description: Sec. 2.1 says SIMP is gradient-based and may converge to local optima, but gives no update scheme, move limit, initial density or convergence tolerance. Sec. 4.1 only names ToPy, and only for the dataset.
readings: OC, move limit 0.2, damping 0.5, uniform start ρ = VF, stop when max density change < 0.01
MMA, uniform start ρ = VF, same tolerance

items.description: The text never says whether any elements are forced solid or void. The load-violation metric (Sec. 4.2) requires material at load points, which may mean solid elements were forced there.
readings: solid element(s) attached to the load node(s)
solid elements at both load and support nodes

items.entity: black-and-white post-processing of the optimized densities
items.description: Sec. 4.1 calls the SIMP ground truth a 'black and white image', which implies binarization, but no threshold rule is given. It is also unclear whether Fig. 1 shows thresholded or raw densities.
readings: threshold chosen to preserve the prescribed volume fraction
